declarations.name: parseUnits
declarations.description: The known units in `list` (space or comma separated), largest first; none known means all four.

declarations.name: splitRemaining
declarations.description:
Splits `remaining` milliseconds over `units`. The smallest unit is rounded up, so the display reads 0 only once the
time is over, and the largest unit absorbs everything above it: with `hours minutes`, two days read as 48 hours.
`trim` drops the leading units that are zero, keeping at least the smallest.

Time left until a date, or through a duration, that keeps itself current. It draws a box per unit (`segments`), a
clock (`clock`, `14:05:31`) or a phrase (`inline`, "2 days 14 hours"), in the units you list, with the unit names and
digits of the element's `locale` (else the nearest `lang`, else the browser's language) from `Intl`, so there is
nothing to translate. One timer per element wakes exactly when the shown value changes: a countdown in hours and
minutes redraws once a minute.

Give it `date` to count down to a moment (an ISO 8601 string or a millisecond timestamp in markup, a `Date` from
script), or `duration` in seconds for a timer that starts when the element connects (unless `paused`). `pause()`,
`start()` and `reset()` drive the timer from script. At zero the element fires `complete` once and shows its `ended`
slot in place of the zeros, if given.

The host has the `timer` role, and a visually hidden phrase ("2 days, 14 hours, 5 minutes") is what assistive
technology reads; the drawn digits are hidden from it. Style its states with `:state(running)`, `:state(paused)`,
`:state(warning)` (less than `warn-at` seconds left) and `:state(ended)`.

members.name: date
members.description: The moment to count down to: an ISO 8601 string or a millisecond timestamp in markup, or a `Date` from script. Wins over `duration`.

members.name: duration
members.description: Length of a timer in seconds, used when `date` is unset. The timer starts when the element connects, unless `paused`; changing it restarts the timer.

members.name: units
members.description: The units to show, largest first, from `days`, `hours`, `minutes` and `seconds`. The largest absorbs the rest: `hours minutes` shows two days as 48 hours.

members.name: display
members.description: `segments` draws a box per unit with its name, `clock` draws `14:05:31`, `inline` writes a phrase such as "2 days 14 hours".

members.name: format
members.description: Length of the unit names: `long` ("hours"), `short` ("hr") or `narrow` ("h").

members.name: trim
members.description: Leave out the leading units that are zero: three hours left read "3 hours 12 minutes", not "0 days 3 hours 12 minutes".

members.name: warnAt
members.description: Seconds left under which the element is in its warning state (`:state(warning)`, coloured by `--c2-countdown__warning--color`). 0 turns it off.

members.name: paused
members.description: Stop the countdown where it is. A timer resumes from the same point; a countdown to a `date` catches up with the time that passed.

members.name: locale
members.description: BCP 47 locale of the unit names and digits. Empty uses the nearest `lang` attribute, then the browser's language.

members.name: #language
members.description: `locale`, else the nearest `lang`, else the browser's language; a `lang` change redraws at once.

members.name: #endsAt
members.description: When a running timer (`duration`) ends, in epoch milliseconds.

members.name: #left
members.description: Time left when the countdown was paused, or before a timer first starts.

members.name: #completed
members.description: Whether `complete` already fired for the current run.

members.name: #lastShown
members.description: The value drawn last, so `tick` fires only when it changes.

members.name: #hasRun
members.description: Whether the element has drawn its countdown running; `complete` fires only after that.

members.name: #date
members.description: `date` parsed, and `units` read, once per update.

members.name: #remaining
members.description: The time left this update draws: one reading of the clock for `render()` and `updated()`, so both agree.

members.name: remaining
members.description: Milliseconds left: 0 once the time is over, and the full length for a timer that has not started.

members.name: start
members.description: Resumes a paused countdown. A timer that ran out starts again from its full `duration`.

members.name: pause
members.description: Stops the countdown where it is; `start()` resumes it.

members.name: reset
members.description: Puts a timer back to its full `duration`, running unless paused, and arms `complete` again. A countdown to a `date` has nothing to reset.

members.name: #nextChangeIn
members.description: Milliseconds until the shown value, or the warning state, changes.

members.name: #unitName
members.description: Unit name for `value` in the element's language: "hours", "hr", "h".

events.name: tick
events.description: Fired whenever the shown value changes; `detail.remaining` is the time left in milliseconds.

events.name: complete
events.description: Fired once when the countdown reaches zero while the element is on the page.
